name: Zhang Xiaolin
current_role: Co-owner (30.97%) of Henan Yintai Investment and co-controller of Henan Yinke International Chemical; director of Henan Yongxin Chemical
profile: Zhang Xiaolin (张晓琳) is the wife of Tan Ruiqing, longtime 5%+ shareholder and former vice-chairman of titanium-dioxide giant Lomon Billions (龙佰集团, 002601.SZ). The couple's wealth stems from their Lomon Billions stake, held directly and via Henan Yintai Investment, which Zhang co-owns. Exchange filings describe Henan Yinke International Chemical as jointly controlled by Tan and Zhang.
interesting_fact: Lomon Billions is one of the world's largest titanium dioxide producers; Tan Ruiqing's stake was about 8.3% in early 2026 before he sold ~1.35% of the company's shares via open-market trades in Feb-Mar 2026.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews or personal channels found. Identity confirmed via SZSE filings naming her as Tan Ruiqing's spouse (http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2022-04-13/1212898666.PDF). Any approach would realistically go via Lomon Billions' board office / Tan Ruiqing. Alive status not explicitly confirmed, though she appears as a shareholder in a March 2026 filing.

name: Viscount Rothermere
current_role: Chairman, Daily Mail and General Trust (DMGT); Chairman, Imperial War Museum Foundation
profile: Jonathan Harmsworth, 4th Viscount Rothermere (b. 1967), is the fourth generation of the Harmsworth family to control DMGT, publisher of the Daily Mail, Mail on Sunday, Metro, the i and MailOnline. He became chairman on his father's death in 1998, took DMGT private in 2021-22, and in Nov 2025 agreed a ~GBP500m deal to buy the Telegraph, which drew a UK public-interest review in 2026.
interesting_fact: DMGT's 2022 delisting ended 90 years on the London Stock Exchange (since 1932); in Nov 2025 DMGT agreed to buy Telegraph Media Group from RedBird IMI at a GBP500m valuation, a deal the Culture Secretary referred for public-interest/competition review in Feb 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs the Imperial War Museum Foundation, continuing a tradition set by his great-grandfather the 1st Viscount; the foundation, set up in 2009, raised funds for IWM London's GBP40m Foster + Partners-designed First World War Galleries, opened in 2014. Before succeeding, he studied history at Duke and ran the Evening Standard as MD in the early 1990s.

public_contacts.value: enquiries@dmgt.com (DMGT general enquiries, Northcliffe House, London)

notes: Rarely gives interviews; Telegraph deal status should be checked for latest regulatory outcome. Best route is DMGT corporate PR. Media-only background, little energy/data-centre angle beyond DMGT's past info businesses (e.g., Trepp, Landmark).

name: Liu Junhui
current_role: Early/pre-IPO shareholder of Walvax Biotechnology (沃森生物, 300142.SZ); private investor
profile: Liu Junhui (刘俊辉) is one of the founding-era shareholders of Kunming-based vaccine maker Walvax Biotechnology, named alongside founder Li Yunchun in its 2010 IPO undertakings and described as its second-largest shareholder in 2015. He held 5.93% in 2019 and has since reduced his stake; by mid-2026 only his wife's holding appeared among the top ten. He also holds private investments, e.g. in a target of Mengwang Technology's 2025 acquisition.
interesting_fact: Walvax developed China's first domestically made 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine; Liu, then a 5%+ holder, announced share sales in 2019 as that vaccine was in registration.
notes: Passive investor with no public profile, interviews or social accounts found; no current board role at Walvax. Wife Huang Jing (黄静) is a co-shareholder (filings: http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2023-05-30/1216940545.PDF). Wealth likely well below the listed figure after sell-downs. Walvax IR is the only published route and is not a personal channel.

name: Charles Sirois
current_role: Chairman and Founder, Telesystem Ltd. (Montreal family holding); Chairman, NorthStar Earth & Space
profile: Charles Sirois (b. 1954, Chicoutimi, Quebec) is a Canadian telecom entrepreneur who built paging firm National Pagette into BCE Mobile, ran Teleglobe, and founded Microcell (Fido) and Telesystem International Wireless. He chaired CIBC 2009-2015 and co-founded the Coalition Avenir Quebec with Francois Legault in 2011. Today his family holding Telesystem invests in media (OnMobile, Zone3, Stingray), space (NorthStar) and cleantech (CVTCorp).
interesting_fact: In 1994 Telesystem and Ted Rogers co-founded Telesystem International Wireless, which expanded into eight countries on three continents; Telesystem also launched Fido (Microcell) in 1996, which passed 1 million subscribers within about four years of its 1997 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: His empire began in 1978 when, aged about 24, he bought out Setelco, a small paging-device business founded by his father in Chicoutimi; it became Telesystem. He also chairs and co-founded the McPeak-Sirois Group for Clinical Research in Breast Cancer, and chairs the board of Montreal engineering school ETS.
notes: Strong podcast fit: telecom/infrastructure builder, energy angle via Telesystem Energy (renewables, run by Denis M. Sirois) and CVTCorp efficient drivetrains, plus satellite data (NorthStar). Son Francois-Charles Sirois is now Telesystem President/CEO. Wikidata net worth (C$1.2bn, 2015) is dated. Team bio: https://telesystem.ca/about-us/team

name: Robert Agostinelli
current_role: Chairman & Co-Founder, Rhone Group (private equity), based in Milan
profile: Robert F. Agostinelli (b. 1953, Rochester, NY) co-founded transatlantic private-equity firm Rhone Group in 1996 with Steven Langman after senior roles at Lazard Freres and Goldman Sachs, where he founded the international M&A business in London. Rhone invests across Europe and North America; he now chairs the firm from Milan and sits on the boards of Illy and Rexair.
interesting_fact: Before Goldman he worked for Lord Jacob Rothschild at RIT in 1981-82, then went on to found Goldman Sachs's international M&A business in London.
deep_cut_fact: The son of Italian immigrants, he went to Rochester's Aquinas Institute and the small St. John Fisher College (BA 1976) and is a qualified CPA; today he chairs the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington and is a trustee of the Lt Michael P. Murphy Navy SEAL Museum.

public_contacts.value: webinfo@rhonegroup.com (Rhone Group general inquiries, via contact page link)
https://www.rhonegroup.com/contact/ (offices New York, London, Madrid, Milan)

notes: Writes op-eds (WSJ, Washington Times) and is active in US conservative/veterans causes. Rhone site blocks scripted access; contact via firm's Milan office per its team page. Wealth estimates (STRL GBP689m 2018; Forbes ~$1bn) are dated.

name: Fan Chi
current_role: Former Alibaba Group vice president (left May 2021); current role not publicly reported
profile: Fan Chi (范驰, Alibaba nickname 'Cheng Yaojin') spent 11 years at Alibaba from Dec 2010, building Alipay's quick-pay and mobile payments, then serving as CEO of Koubei (2015), president of Fliggy (2019) and head of OTT/sports at Alibaba Digital Media & Entertainment (2020). His wealth came from Alibaba/Ant equity; he left the group on 1 May 2021 and has kept a low profile since.
interesting_fact: In June 2015 he became CEO of Koubei, the local-services joint venture of Alibaba and Ant Financial, which later merged with Ele.me after Alibaba bought it in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: His longest stint at Alibaba was at Alipay, where he worked across 'kuaijie' express payment, wireless payment and the Alipay app, holding brand, marketing, operations and product roles before Koubei.
notes: No public post-2021 activity, personal website or social accounts found; only appeared on Hurun in 2017. Any approach would have to go through mutual Alibaba-alumni networks. Not verified whether he was a formal Alibaba Partnership member.
